summary: Split the one gated preview into two, so the link the team reviews stops moving while work is in progress. `main` is now the reviewed site and only advances when someone promotes; `staging` is the working site and takes every commit. Both are hosted on GitHub Pages URLs, so harvardintech.com is not touched until the Strikingly migration is approved.

changes.title: A staging site that needs no DNS
changes.description: The deploy workflow already had a dormant staging job, but it targeted review.harvardintech.com — which would mean adding a DNS record to a domain we do not yet have permission to touch. It now builds for nseldeib.github.io/harvardintech-staging instead: a base path matching the repo, PAGES_SITE on github.io, and no CNAME file. A CNAME here would bind a domain whose DNS points elsewhere, and GitHub Pages would serve a misconfigured-domain error rather than the site. The three-line diff that moves it onto the real subdomain at cutover is recorded inline, so the deferral is a note in the file rather than folklore.

waysToTest.text: Read src/lib/deployTracks.test.ts — the `deploy.yml track coherence` block asserts the staging base path matches the repo it publishes to, and that no CNAME is written.

Build it the way CI will: DEPLOY_BASE_PATH=/harvardintech-staging PAGES_SITE=https://nseldeib.github.io PREVIEW_GATE=1 INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1 npx astro build — then check dist/index.html links start with /harvardintech-staging/, dist/admin exists, and dist/CNAME does not.

tests.name: deploy.yml track coherence › builds the staging track with a base matching the repo it publishes to
tests.description: The base path and the push target sit far apart in the workflow with nothing connecting them; a mismatch deploys a site that returns 200 while every asset 404s.

tests.name: deploy.yml track coherence › writes no CNAME on the staging track
tests.description: A stray CNAME would bind a domain whose DNS does not point here, and Pages would serve a misconfigured-domain error instead of the site.

tests.name: deploy.yml track coherence › gates both tracks while neither is meant to be public
tests.description: Dropping PREVIEW_GATE is exactly what takes a site public, and harvardintech.com is still Strikingly's — so until the cutover both tracks must set it.

tests.name: deploy.yml track coherence › builds the reviewed track with a base matching this repo
tests.description: The same base-path rule applies to main, which this change deliberately leaves untouched — the assertion pins that it stayed correct.

changes.title: The base-path rule, extracted and guarded
changes.description: A GitHub Pages project site is served at <user>.github.io/<repo>/, so its Astro base must be /<repo>. That correspondence previously existed only as two hand-matched strings in the workflow. `pagesBasePathFor` states the rule and `pushTargetRepo` reads the repo back out of the job's git push line, so the contract test can compare the two halves rather than restating a literal that would itself drift. This is the same bug class landing-images.test.ts was written after, one level up: a wrong base ships a site that looks fine and 404s everything.

waysToTest.text: Read src/lib/deployTracks.test.ts — 11 unit cases across both functions covering typical input, surrounding slashes and whitespace, SSH and HTTPS remotes, a hyphenated owner, and the empty and no-remote cases.
Confirm the guard actually bites: delete the DEPLOY_BASE_PATH line from the staging job and re-run the test file — two assertions go red and the rest stay green.

tests.name: pagesBasePathFor › returns the repo name as a rooted path
tests.description: The rule itself: a project site at <user>.github.io/<repo>/ builds with base /<repo>.

example.note: The value deploy.yml must set as DEPLOY_BASE_PATH for that repo.

tests.name: pagesBasePathFor › throws on an empty repo name rather than returning a bare slash
tests.description: A bare slash is the base of a user site or custom domain, so returning it for an empty repo would build every asset URL wrong while looking entirely plausible.

example.note: A bare '/' would be the base of a user site or custom domain — plausible-looking and wrong.

tests.name: pagesBasePathFor › tolerates surrounding slashes rather than doubling them
tests.description: Someone copying the repo name the way it appears in a URL should not end up with a doubled slash.

tests.name: pushTargetRepo › reads the repo out of an SSH push command
tests.description: The exact form the staging job uses, so the contract test reads the real value rather than a restated literal.

example.note: The exact push line the staging job runs.

tests.name: pushTargetRepo › returns the repo, not the owner
tests.description: A hyphenated owner must not be mistaken for the repo name.

tests.name: pushTargetRepo › returns undefined when the command contains no remote
tests.description: A step that pushes nowhere is a real state — the reviewed track publishes by artifact upload — so it is reported rather than thrown on.

example.note: The reviewed track publishes by artifact upload and has no remote at all.

changes.title: Docs that describe what exists, not what was planned
changes.description: Five documents described review.harvardintech.com as though it were live, and CMS_SETUP.md was actively wrong: it said CMS commits go to the staging branch when cms.json names main. They now describe today's two gated sites and mark the DNS arrangement as the post-migration end state. DEPLOY_SETUP.md's setup section became a live checklist with the completed steps ticked and the real blocker recorded — GitHub Pages refuses private repos on a free plan, which is why the staging repo is public. The handoff doc gains a section naming which of the two links is Nicole's, plus a note that her CMS edits land on main and will make the next promote open a PR instead of fast-forwarding.

waysToTest.text: Prose has no unit test. Read DEPLOY_SETUP.md top to bottom: the two-site table, the cutover diff, and the four-step setup checklist should each match what the deploy workflow actually does.
